title: Authenticated forwarded data can poison passive gradients for spoofed IPv6 sources
description: Security review of python/src/lichen/node.py found the FORWARD path installs a DATA gradient for packet.header.src_addr via rx.sender without any source-identity or route-origin evidence. Link authentication proves only the immediate sender, so an admitted peer can send a packet claiming an arbitrary absent victim 02xx source and install a 60-second route toward itself; the update occurs even before next-hop identity/compression/transmission succeeds. This enables blackholing/interception until an explicit higher-priority route arrives. Define the authorization/evidence required for passive learning (or keep it quarantined from forwarding decisions), bind learning to successful forwarding and authenticated provenance, and add spoofed-source/non-forwarded-packet regressions.
